other.label: CBO cost estimate: H.R. 5301, PIPES Act of 2025

summary: The PIPES Act of 2025 amends title 49 of the United States Code to enhance safety in pipeline transportation, update regulations, authorize appropriations for pipeline safety programs, and expand federal oversight to include carbon dioxide pipeline facilities and storage.

affected_groups.effect: Subject to updated safety standards, expanded carbon dioxide pipeline regulations, vapor dispersion modeling requirements, revised maximum allowable operating pressure testing rules, increased civil penalties, and new criminal penalties for intentionally damaging infrastructure, while gaining access to a voluntary information-sharing system and alternative rights-of-way management options.
affected_groups.group: Pipeline Owners and Operators (Gas, Hazardous Liquid, and Carbon Dioxide)

affected_groups.effect: Eligible to apply for federal grants to repair, rehabilitate, or replace high-risk or leaking municipal and community-owned natural gas distribution infrastructure, with priority given to rural or economically distressed areas.
affected_groups.group: Publicly Owned Natural Gas Distribution Systems and Municipalities

affected_groups.effect: Receives authorized appropriations for operations and grants, authorization to hire up to 30 additional full-time employees with technical expertise, new periodic reporting requirements on outstanding rulemaking mandates, and expanded enforcement and inspection duties regarding carbon dioxide and LNG facilities.
affected_groups.group: Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration (PHMSA) and Federal/State Regulators

affected_groups.effect: Eligible for a 100-percent Federal share of financial assistance under the Competitive Academic Agreement Program if they have total enrollments of 17,500 students or less and submit a written request.

key_provisions: Authorizes appropriations and grants for gas, hazardous liquid, and underground natural gas storage safety programs, operational expenses, one-call notification programs, and community safety grants from fiscal years 2026 through 2029.

Establishes a new grant program (Safe Energy for Communities Updating and Replacing Infrastructure for Natural Gas Systems) to assist publicly owned natural gas distribution pipeline systems in repairing or replacing high-risk or leaking pipelines, funded at $150 million annually for fiscal years 2027 through 2029.

Expands definitions and regulatory authority under chapter 601 to comprehensively cover carbon dioxide pipelines, carbon dioxide storage incidental to pipeline transportation, and interstate and intrastate carbon dioxide facilities.

Requires the Secretary of Transportation to establish a confidential, voluntary information-sharing system (VIS) governed by a board of stakeholders to share pipeline safety data and lessons learned in a non-punitive context.

Increases maximum civil penalties for pipeline safety violations to $3,412,000 and establishes a criminal penalty of up to 10 years in prison or fines for knowingly and willfully causing a defect in or disrupting the operation of pipeline infrastructure.

Directs various studies, reports, and reviews by the Comptroller General, the National Academies, and the Secretary of Transportation on topics such as composite pipeline materials, geohazard mitigation, hydrogen blending, integrity management, and the costs of pipeline failures.

summary_detail.plain_summary: The PIPES Act of 2025 amends title 49 of the United States Code to enhance safety in pipeline transportation, update regulations, authorize appropriations for pipeline safety programs, and expand federal oversight to include carbon dioxide pipeline facilities and storage.
summary_detail.significance: The bill updates and expands federal pipeline safety laws by incorporating carbon dioxide pipelines into the federal regulatory framework, increasing funding for infrastructure modernization and safety grants, establishing a confidential safety information-sharing system, and setting higher financial and criminal penalties for safety violations.
